tagline: Global hospitality leader with asset-light franchise model
hero_kpi_rationale: Fee Revenue represents the core of IHG's business model, generating high-margin recurring cash flows through franchisees. This metric directly reflects network growth and operator confidence in IHG brands.

kpis.name: Fee Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned from partner hotels that pay fees to use IHG's brand and services.
kpis.description: Fee revenues represent the majority of IHG's operating revenues and reflect confidence from independent operators in its global brands.
kpis.signal: Solid growth on a recurring, high-margin model

kpis.name: Operating Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit after operating costs but before taxes and interest.
kpis.description: Operating profitability advanced due to fee revenue growth and rigorous cost management.
kpis.signal: Improvement in operational efficiency despite inflationary backdrop

kpis.name: Underlying Fee Operating Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit generated from fee activities, excluding FX effects and exceptional items.
kpis.description: This KPI shows the real performance of IHG's core business model, net of currency fluctuations.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total money earned by IHG during the year.
kpis.description: Total revenue includes fees, hotel management, and insurance activities.
kpis.signal: Stable growth driven by network expansion

kpis.name: EMEA Revenue Growth
kpis.explanation: Percentage progression of revenues in the Europe, Middle East and Africa region.
kpis.description: The EMEA region showed the fastest growth, driven by robust residential and corporate travel demand.

kpis.name: Greater China Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenues generated in the Greater China region.
kpis.description: China revenues are stable, indicating a plateau after the strong 2023 recovery.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €5.34 Bn in latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €4.61 Bn in latest year

kpis.name: Underlying Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue adjusted for FX effects and divestitures.
kpis.description: Underlying revenue shows solid performance excluding non-recurring impacts.

kpis.name: EMEA Operating Profit Growth
kpis.explanation: Percentage progression of operating profit in Europe, Middle East and Africa.
kpis.description: EMEA profitability surged due to strong occupancy and cost management.

risks.title: Pipeline growth conversion dependency and conversion risk
risks.score_rationale: Core business risk: 2,292-hotel pipeline depends on conversion and continuous signings. Prominent positioning in report (pages 6-7, 9-13). Moderate language but explicit acknowledgment that growth relies on ability to convert signings into openings. Stable trend but dependent on volatile geopolitical and economic conditions mentioned.

risks.title: Geographic concentration and region-specific risks
risks.score_rationale: Explicit business risk: Chair statement mentions 'challenging economic and geopolitical environment' (page 4). Regional data shows Greater China dependency (-1.6% RevPAR in 2025, page 9) and EMEAA exposure. Alert language on 'macro-economic and geopolitical uncertainty and conflict' (page 5). Uptrend: escalating geopolitical tensions affect all three regions.

risks.title: Critical dependency on IHG One Rewards loyalty program
risks.score_rationale: Strategic business risk: program described as 'critical to our business and future growth' (page 6). 160 million members generating 66% of global nights (pages 6, 9). Language of critical importance. Stable trend but growing dependency. Any technological disruption or member loss would directly impact revenues.

risks.title: Technological transformation and AI adoption risk
risks.score_rationale: Explicit business risk: Chair statement identifies 'ability to properly harness transformational technological change' as 'essential in driving competitive advantage' (page 4). Board focus areas include 'effective and responsible use of artificial intelligence' (page 5). Language of strategic importance. Uptrend: AI flagged as new priority in 2025.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and IT risk management
risks.score_rationale: Explicit business risk: Board focus areas include 'cybersecurity risk management, including assessing threats and recovery plans' (page 5). Formal alert language. Digital platform is critical (160M members, 66% of bookings) creating major attack surface. Stable trend but growing importance with digitalization.

risks.title: Intense competition and brand portfolio fragmentation
risks.score_rationale: Implicit business risk: IHG has 20 brands (Ruby acquisition in 2025, page 13) and acknowledges need for 'broad portfolio of distinct brands' to 'meet evolving needs' (page 4). Moderate language but recognition that diversification is competitive response. Stable trend: established portfolio strategy.

risks.title: Franchise model dependency and owner quality risks
risks.score_rationale: Structural business risk: 'asset-light, fee-based, predominantly franchised' model (page 4) means dependency on independent owners for quality and compliance. Report mentions 'thousands of owners' (pages 4-5) but limited detail on non-compliance risks. Stable trend: established model but inherent risk.

risks.title: Environmental regulation and sustainability obligations
risks.score_rationale: Growing business risk: report details sustainability initiatives (pages 70-73): 10.2% energy reduction, 11.0% carbon reduction, but acknowledges 'total carbon emissions increased 7.7%' despite efforts (page 10). Language of commitment but tension between growth and environmental targets. Uptrend: environmental regulation accelerating globally.

ai_positioning.summary: IHG explores AI to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency, but without major transformation announcement. Focus remains on network expansion and progressive digitalization.
evidence: AI use in booking engines to personalize offers
Chatbot testing for customer service in select markets
No mention of massive investments or clear AI strategy in report
